patches.rationale: The current implementation uses zero-based indexing (start = page * page_size), so page=2, size=2 on range(1,8) returns items[4:6] == [5,6]. The issue requires one-based page numbers: page 1 -> first page, page 2 -> second page. Fix: start = (page - 1) * page_size. Empty/invalid inputs already return [] (page<1 or page_size<1), and slicing beyond the end naturally returns []. Add a new regression test file covering the stated contracts.

edits.old:
start = page * page_size
    return items[start : start + page_size]
edits.new:
start = (page - 1) * page_size
    return items[start : start + page_size]

patches.rationale: The paginate function already uses one-based page numbering (start = (page-1)*page_size), but it returns a slice of the input, which for a range input is a range object, not a list. The issue's contract requires paginate(range(1,8), 2, 2) to return [3,4] — a list. The failing tests show actual results like range(3,5) vs expected [3,4]. The fix is to materialize the slice as a list. This preserves empty/invalid input behavior (returns []) and beyond-last-page behavior (empty slice -> []). Existing test_contract.py assertions (paginate([],1,2)==[] and paginate([1,2],0,2)==[]) still pass since [] == [] and list slicing of a list already returns a list. The new regression test file already exists and covers the contracts; I will not modify it (immutable).
contract_tests: tests/test_pagination_regression.py::test_page_two_size_two_returns_third_and_fourth asserts paginate(range(1, 8), 2, 2) == [3, 4] and isinstance(result, list) — one-based page numbering with list result type.
tests/test_pagination_regression.py::test_first_page_returns_first_items asserts paginate(range(1, 8), 1, 2) == [1, 2] — page 1 returns first size items.
tests/test_pagination_regression.py::test_last_partial_page_returns_remaining_item asserts paginate(range(1, 8), 4, 2) == [7] — last partial page returns remaining item.
tests/test_pagination_regression.py::test_page_beyond_last_page_returns_empty asserts paginate(range(1, 8), 5, 2) == [] — beyond last page returns [].
tests/test_pagination_regression.py::test_negative_page_and_size_return_empty asserts paginate([1, 2, 3], -1, 2) == [] and paginate([1, 2, 3], 1, -2) == [] — negative inputs return [].
tests/test_contract.py::test_existing_contract asserts paginate([], 1, 2) == [] and paginate([1, 2], 0, 2) == [] — existing public contract preserved.
